back: The gap between the highest price a buyer will pay (bid) and the lowest price a seller will accept (ask). You typically buy at the ask and sell at the bid, so the spread is a cost.
An instruction to fill immediately at the best available prices. Speed over price. Slippage can be large in thin books.
An instruction to buy or sell only at a specified price or better. Price control, but it may not fill.
The largest peak-to-trough drop in an equity curve. A risk metric, not a return metric.
Average excess return per unit of volatility, often annualized. It is sensitive to sample length and does not capture crash risk well.

front: Why model returns instead of raw prices?
back: Price levels depend on scale and are usually non-stationary. Simple returns (pct change) compare relative moves.
Using information that would not have been available at the decision time (future bars, restated data, shuffled time series).

front: Why include transaction costs in a paper backtest?
back: A rule that looks profitable at 0 bps often dies after spread, fees, and slippage. Turnover is expensive.
Train on an earlier window, test on the next unused window, then roll forward. One in-sample score is not evidence.

front: Name one sign a backtest is overfit.
back: Many free parameters, no costs, random train/test on time, or a strategy that only works on one ticker and one window.

front: What is the Kelly fraction in this repo?
back: An educational formula f* = p - (1-p)/b. It is a probability identity, not a live betting or position-sizing system.

front: What is FOMO as a trading bias?
back: Entering because others seem to be winning, not because a pre-committed rule fired. Common journal miss; worth a flashcard, not a signal.
No. They are vocabulary and research hygiene. Software here does not place orders and does not claim an edge.

front: A gap opens through a stop. What risk idea is that?
back: Stops are instructions, not guarantees. Gaps and illiquid prints can fill far from the stop price.

front: What belongs in a paper-trade checklist card?
back: Horizon, max loss, cost assumption, and what would falsify the idea — reviewed before a mock session, not after.
